content: {"rules": ["Correct for severe underestimation of short-term volatility: The model consistently forecasts smooth, monotonic trends while true outcomes exhibit sharp spikes (e.g., +10-12 EUR) followed by rapid mean reversion; apply a volatility multiplier to the first 5-7 days of the forecast horizon.", "Implement aggressive mean reversion after sentiment spikes: When sentiment history shows consecutive high values (1.00) followed by a price spike, the model fails to anticipate the subsequent crash; reduce the forecast slope by 40-50% immediately after the peak to align with the observed 15-20 EUR correction.", "Adjust for sentiment lag in trend reversal: The model reacts too slowly to negative sentiment shifts (e.g., -0.50 or -1.00) appearing in the history; if recent sentiment turns negative, force an immediate downward adjustment to the forecast trajectory rather than maintaining the historical upward drift.", "Reduce long-horizon bias: The model exhibits a persistent upward bias in the 20-30 day window regardless of the actual price level; flatten the forecast curve in the second half of the horizon to prevent overestimation of the terminal price.", "Decouple forecast from recent price momentum: The model over-relies on the immediate past price trend (momentum) and ignores the structural mean-reverting nature of the EU ETS; if the last 3 days show a sharp rise, the forecast should not continue rising linearly but should plateau or decline."]}
